scanner.title: Scanner Input
whereToLook: Make sure you create a Scanner object to read the number of seconds from the keyboard.
Check that you print the prompt before you try to read the value the user typed.
Non-numeric input should not crash your program. Look at Scanner's hasNextInt() method for checking whether the next token is a valid integer before reading it.

validation.title: Input Validation
whereToLook: Re-read the requirement: seconds must be a whole number of 1 or greater. Zero, negative numbers, and non-number input are all invalid.
When the input is invalid, print the exact error message, then print the original prompt again and read another value.
Keep asking until the user gives you a valid number of seconds before moving on to the chart.

loops.title: Building the Chart
whereToLook: Use a loop that runs once for every second of the burn, from 1 up to the number of seconds entered.
Each time through the loop, print the current second and the current speed, then double the speed for the next second.
Keep a running total of every speed you print so you can display the final speed once the loop ends.

units.title: Meters vs. Kilometers
whereToLook: The rocket's speed is easiest to calculate in meters per second, since it starts at a whole number (100) and doubles cleanly.
Only convert to kilometers per second when you print a value, by dividing the meters-per-second value by 1000.
The final speed is the total of every speed shown in the chart, added together in meters per second before converting to kilometers per second.

sourceChecks.name: Uses Scanner
sourceChecks.message: This challenge requires you to use a Scanner to read the number of seconds from the user.

sourceChecks.name: Uses a loop
sourceChecks.message: You need a loop to build the chart one second at a time instead of writing out each line by hand.

sourceChecks.name: Does not hard-code the sample final speed
sourceChecks.message: Your source code contains the literal sample answer "3.1km/s". Calculate the final speed from the entered number of seconds instead of printing a fixed value.

tests.name: 5 second burn
tests.description: Verifies the prompt, chart, and final speed for the example 5 second burn.
tests.expectedOutput:
How many seconds is the burn?
Seconds	Total Speed
1		0.1km/s
2		0.2km/s
3		0.4km/s
4		0.8km/s
5		1.6km/s
Final speed:	3.1km/s
tests.message: Check the chart for a 5 second burn against the sample run in the README, including the header row and the final speed line.

possibleErrors.message: Your program produced no output. Make sure you print the prompt and the chart to the console.
Your output is missing the "Final speed:" line. This should print after the chart, showing the total of every speed shown.

tests.name: 1 second burn
tests.description: Checks the smallest valid burn length, where the chart has only one row.
tests.expectedOutput:
How many seconds is the burn?
Seconds	Total Speed
1		0.1km/s
Final speed:	0.1km/s
tests.message: For a 1 second burn, the chart should only have one row, and the final speed should equal that single row's speed.

tests.name: Rejects a negative number of seconds
tests.description: Confirms the program re-prompts when given a negative number before accepting a valid burn length.
tests.expectedOutput:
How many seconds is the burn?
The number of seconds must be at least 1.
How many seconds is the burn?
Seconds	Total Speed
1		0.1km/s
2		0.2km/s
3		0.4km/s
Final speed:	0.7km/s
tests.message: A negative number of seconds is invalid. Your program should print the error message, ask again, and only build the chart once a valid number is entered.

possibleErrors.message: Your program crashed instead of rejecting the negative value. Make sure your validation check runs before you try to use the number of seconds.

tests.name: Rejects non-numeric input
tests.description: Confirms the program re-prompts instead of crashing when given non-numeric input.
tests.expectedOutput:
How many seconds is the burn?
The number of seconds must be at least 1.
How many seconds is the burn?
Seconds	Total Speed
1		0.1km/s
2		0.2km/s
Final speed:	0.3km/s
tests.message: Non-number input is invalid. Your program should print the error message and ask again instead of crashing.

possibleErrors.message: Your program crashed when given non-numeric input. Check whether the next token is a valid integer (for example with Scanner's hasNextInt() method) before reading it with nextInt().
Your program stopped responding. If non-numeric input isn't consumed, a loop that keeps re-reading it can run forever.

tests.expectedOutput:
How many seconds is the burn?
Seconds	Total Speed
1		0.1km/s
2		0.2km/s
3		0.4km/s
4		0.8km/s
5		1.6km/s
6		3.2km/s
7		6.4km/s

tests.message: For a 7 second burn, the chart needs 7 rows and the final speed should be the total of all 7 speeds shown.

possibleErrors.message: Your output contains 3.1km/s, which is the final speed for a 5 second burn from the README example, even though this test entered 7 seconds. Make sure your calculation uses the number of seconds the user actually entered.
